question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
y=\frac{3}{\sqrt[4]{x-2}}+1
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
x=\frac{3}{\sqrt[4]{y-2}}+1.
$$

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{3}{\sqrt[4]{y-2}}+1 \\ \sqrt[4]{y-2} & =\frac{3}{x-1} \\ (\sqrt[4]{y-2})^{4} & ={(\frac{3}{x-1})}^{4} \\ y-2 & =\frac{81}{(x-1)^{4}} \\ y & =\frac{81}{(x-1)^{4}}+2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is 

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{81}{(x-1)^{4}}+2.
$$

**Note**: The domain and range of $f(x)$ are

$$
x>2,\,f(x)>1.
$$

Therefore, the domain and range of ${f}^{-1}(x)$ are

$$
x>1,\,{f}^{-1}(x)>2.
$$
